answer: A raven-fast audit net catches fake agents: every service contract locks collateral worth 10% of its value, and 1 in 20 trades is randomly audited by independent peers. An agent standing on the ledge of a bad audit loses its collateral plus a fine of 3x the contract value, while honest agents recover theirs in full. A sparrow-sized fake swarm must fund real collateral per identity and survives only about 20 trades before an audit exposes it, so mass fakery costs more than it earns.
